facts.rationale: Corrects the low-nibble claim: SET_REG_FIELD uses size 4 and shift 4 for GP selection, whereas vertex-cache attribute selection uses shift 0.
facts.value: The previous selections come from gx->perf0 and gx->perf1 and determine which hardware selector is reset. The arguments then replace those shadow fields and are translated into XF register 6 values, BP/rasterizer command words, bits 4–7 of gx->perfSel, or command-processor register 3 values. The perfSel update preserves its low nibble, which GXSetVCacheMetric updates separately. GXReadGPMetric later dispatches on the stored selections to interpret the physical counters, and GXSetGPMetric clears gx->bpSent after programming.

evidence.why: Selection transitions, assertion branches and bpSent update.
Counter-specific guards, reset operations and shared XF/raster hardware configuration.

facts.rationale: Replaces the blanket read/clear prohibition with the actual per-routine guards and preserves the shared-hardware/cache lifetime distinction.
facts.value: GP selection disables sources associated with the old cached selectors before storing and programming replacements. NONE performs no new selector write; invalid old or new selectors reach assertions. GP reads/clears, memory reads/clears, and pixel reads assert against display-list construction. This restriction is not a universal local guard: pixel clear uses CHECK_GXBEGIN and emits rasterizer commands, while vertex-cache and XF/raster reads have no local display-list assertion. GP clear writes 4 to __cpReg[2] without changing selections. GP selection and XF/raster initialization set bpSent to 0, whereas pixel clear sets it to 1. XF/raster initialization reuses GP selector hardware without updating gx->perf0 or gx->perf1.
